architecture: XGBoost Regressor + Split-Conformal Inference + ONNX Runtime CPU
dataset: NASA C-MAPSS FD001 (Single operating condition, sea-level turbofan)
task: Remaining Useful Life (RUL) Prognostics with Calibrated Uncertainty Bounds
features: Causal rolling mean/std/slope over windows [5, 10, 30] + min-max normalisation + cycle index
validation_method: 5-Fold GroupKFold grouped by engine_id (zero cross-engine data leakage)
limitations: Sim-to-real gap: Trained on C-MAPSS thermodynamic simulation (1990s digital model), not flight telemetry.
Single flight regime: FD001 models sea-level steady flight; multi-condition transitions (FD002/004) require altitude/mach condition clustering.
Sensor drift assumption: Assumes healthy sensor baselines during early flight cycles (1..30). Degradation of sensor hardware itself is not modeled.
Piecewise linear RUL: Target clipped at 125 cycles assumption — early cycles assume constant health.
citations: Saxena et al. (2008), Damage Propagation Modeling for Aircraft Engine Run-to-Failure Simulation (NASA C-MAPSS benchmark)
Vovk et al. (2005), Algorithmic Learning in a Random World (Conformal Prediction)
Lundberg & Lee (2017), A Unified Approach to Interpreting Model Predictions (SHAP)
